agent_display_name.description: Display name used by the external agent at runtime after trimming. Must be 1-255 characters.

CreateThreadRequest.description:
Create a private thread. Two shapes are accepted and are mutually exclusive:

1. Direct create: supply `kind` and `participants`. Both fields are required in this shape.
2. Branched-from-source create: supply `source_thread_id` (and optional `additional_participants`). In this shape `kind` and `participants` MUST be omitted — the server seeds a new Group thread from the source thread's active participants plus `additional_participants`.

Mixing the two shapes (e.g. sending both `kind` and `source_thread_id`) returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

additional_participants.description:
Only valid when `source_thread_id` is set. Optional list of participants to add on top of the seeded set.
Dedup on actor id. May be empty when the caller is branching themselves into the new group.

kind.description: Required for direct create. Must be omitted when `source_thread_id` is set.

participants.description: Required for direct create. Must be omitted when `source_thread_id` is set.

source_thread_id.description:
When set, create a new Group thread seeded from the source thread's active participants plus `additional_participants`.
The caller must have visibility of the source thread (active participant OR owner of an active live agent participant).
The source thread is not modified. Mutually exclusive with `kind` and `participants`.

Error mapping:
- Caller is already an active human participant in source AND `additional_participants` is empty → `400 ALREADY_PARTICIPATING`.
- Caller has no visibility anchor on source → `403 FORBIDDEN`.
- Source not found → `404 THREAD_NOT_FOUND`.
- Sent together with `kind`/`participants` → `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

details.description:
Free-form diagnostic payload. Known shapes:
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` on `POST /api/v1/chat/threads` (DM partial-failure): `details.results` is an array of `ThreadInviteResult` — one entry per requested participant, with `status ∈ {added, already_participating, failed}` and `code` populated on failure (e.g. `NOT_FOUND`). DM partial-failure occurs when any target is `NOT_FOUND` (agent missing/inactive/suspended/deleted, or unknown user) and the transaction is rolled back, so no thread row is committed.

results.description: Per-target invite outcomes, present on DM partial-failure rollback (422) and on group create responses.

ThreadDetailResponse.description: Expanded thread view used by GET /chat/threads/{thread_id}. Includes a first page of messages alongside participants and any attached inquiries.

ThreadEvent.description:
A durable thread event delivered via the **HTTP poll** + **SSE** transports
(this schema scope). `thread_seq` is the per-thread monotonic int64 cursor
assigned by the database trigger on commit; clients pass the highest observed
value back as `last_thread_seq` (HTTP poll) or as the SSE position cursor on
reconnect to resume without duplicates.

WebSocket replay (`/api/v1/chat/ws/threads?since_seq=`) emits an envelope
`{type:"thread_message", data:{...}}` whose `data.message` payload mirrors the
`ThreadEvent` fields but is wrapped — see the WS-route description for the
full taxonomy (`thread_message` / `thread_typing` / `thread_runtime` / `pong`).
WS-only ephemeral frames (`thread_typing`, `pong`) are NOT durable and never
replayed by `since_seq`.

actor_kind.description:
Wire-vocabulary actor kind ("user" or "agent"), captured from the row's
internal sender_id BEFORE the prefix strip so consumers do not need to
re-derive it. Always present at the wire boundary on iter10+ (defaults
to "user" when the sender_id has no recognized prefix). Listed in
`required` because the backend never omits this field on emitted
frames; the iter10+ guarantee holds across all five transports
(HTTP poll, SSE, WS-live, WS-replay, webhook). Pre-iter10 cached
events on the consumer side may still lack the field — strict
validators consuming durable cache snapshots SHOULD treat that
shape as a separate legacy schema (not a violation of this
contract).

client_message_id.description:
Echoed only when the original sender supplied one on the message-submit
payload. Optimistic-send clients use this to reconcile their placeholder
bubble with the server-committed message without an extra round-trip.
Omitted entirely when no `client_message_id` was supplied; `null` is
never emitted.

event_type.description:
Event type literal. HTTP poll / SSE emit `message_committed`. WebSocket
replay + live emit `thread_message` for the same payload shape (see SDK
normalizer `public/sdk/ts/src/wsClient.ts`). Both literals
map to the durable visible-message event. Other WS-only literals
(`thread_typing`, `thread_runtime`, `pong`) are documented in the
WS-route taxonomy table at `services/backend-go/docs/api/chat.md` and
are not part of the durable HTTP/SSE schema.

metadata.description:
Always emitted as an object. `null` is reserved and currently never
sent — empty/missing DB values are surfaced as `{}` for cross-transport
parity (HTTP poll, SSE, WS replay, WS live, webhook).

role.description:
Persisted message role. Always present on iter10+ (defaults to "user"
when the DB row stored an empty value); pre-iter10 wire frames may
omit this field.

sender_id.description:
Pure UUID of the sender at the wire boundary (WU-E2). HTTP poll matches WS
replay/live: routing prefixes (`user:`, `agent:`, `iat:`, `eat:`, `guest:`)
are stripped at the wire-emission layer for cross-transport parity.
WebSocket frames also carry an `actor` object
(`{kind: user|agent, id: <uuid>, display_name?}`) for richer consumer dispatch.

thread_seq.description:
Per-thread monotonic catch-up cursor. Assigned by `trg_assign_thread_seq` on
durable message commit. Pass the highest seen value back as `last_thread_seq`
(HTTP poll / SSE) or `since_seq` (WebSocket) on reconnect to resume without
duplicates.

actor_kind.description:
Wire-vocabulary actor kind ("user" or "agent") derived from
the row's prefixed sender_id — exposed even on this legacy-
shape endpoint so consumers can switch off actor_kind instead
of prefix-sniffing. Optional: omitted when the legacy sender
has no recognized prefix (Go runtime uses `omitempty`).
`null` is never emitted.

client_message_id.description:
Echoed when the sender supplied one on submit. Allows
optimistic-send clients to reconcile their placeholder
bubble. Omitted when the sender did not supply one;
`null` is never emitted.

sender_id.description:
Legacy prefixed shape for the `/threads/{id}/messages` endpoint
(e.g. `"user:<uuid>"`, `"agent:<uuid>"`, `"guest:<email>"`).
Preserved for back-compat with existing web/mobile clients.
Other event APIs (HTTP poll `/events`, SSE, WebSocket) emit the
pure-UUID stripped shape per DC-007. New consumers should
prefer `actor_kind` to discriminate caller-kind without
prefix-aware string parsing.

thread_seq.description:
Per-thread monotonic seq assigned by the database trigger on commit.
Mirrored on WebSocket fanout `data.message.thread_seq` and the
envelope-level `data.thread_seq` for catch-up cursor advancement.
Omitted on legacy fixtures that predate the trigger; `null` is
never emitted.

ThreadMessagesResponse.description: Page of thread messages in reverse-chronological order, scoped to the calling identity's visibility.

results.description: Per-target invite results. Present on create/invite responses; omitted for plain participants reads.

ThreadSummary.description: Summary row returned by GET /chat/threads. Participant set already has the caller filtered out for DMs to match the rendering convention used by the reference UI.

callback_url.description: HTTPS URL invoked when thread events are committed. Private/loopback addresses are rejected (SSRF guard).

UpdateMeRequest.description:
Mixed-auth optimistic profile update request.

Caller-specific field rules:
- user JWT callers may update `display_name`, `username`, and `avatar_url`
- external-agent callers may update `display_name`, `avatar_url`, and `description`

`updated_at` is always required, at least one mutable field must be
present, caller-kind-incompatible fields are rejected, and `username`
plus `description` may not be sent together.

internalAPIKey.description: Internal service-to-service API key. Use together with `X-Sender-ID`.
internalAPIKey.name: X-Internal-API-Key

senderIDHeader.description: Internal caller identity header. Use together with `X-Internal-API-Key`.
senderIDHeader.name: X-Sender-ID

info.title: AMA2 Public Runtime API

get.summary: List threads visible to the authenticated user

post.description:
Two shapes are supported (see `CreateThreadRequest`):

- Direct create: `kind` + `participants`.
- Branched-from-source create: `source_thread_id` (+ optional `additional_participants`). Creates a new `kind=group` thread seeded from the source thread's active participants plus `additional_participants`. The source thread is not modified. Caller must have visibility of source (active participant OR owner of an active live agent participant). Concurrent branch calls may create distinct new groups (no server-side dedup).

400.description:
Request cannot be applied. Error codes include:
- `GROUP_REQUIRES_MIN_3` when `kind=group` and the post-filter active participant count would drop below three (e.g. targets that do not resolve to an existing user or active agent fail and leave fewer than three eligible participants). `details.results` carries per-target outcomes so the caller can render which targets failed.
- `ALREADY_PARTICIPATING` when branching from source (`source_thread_id` set) and the caller is already an active human participant in the source thread AND `additional_participants` is empty.
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` when the branched-from-source and direct-create shapes are mixed (e.g. sending both `kind`/`participants` and `source_thread_id`), or for malformed body / invalid participant shape.

403.description: Caller is not permitted to create this thread (e.g. owner-invocation denied). For branched-from-source create, `FORBIDDEN` is returned when the caller has no visibility anchor on the source thread.

404.description: For branched-from-source create (`source_thread_id` set), the source thread does not exist — `THREAD_NOT_FOUND`.

409.description: Conflicting thread already exists for the participant set

422.description: Validation error (malformed body / invalid participant shape). DM partial-failure rollback also surfaces here via `details.results`.

post.summary: Create or reuse a private thread

get.description: Returns participants, inquiries, and an initial page of messages. Only user JWT callers are currently accepted on this surface.

403.description: Caller is not authorized for this thread

get.description:
Poll committed visible thread events using the durable `thread_seq` cursor.
Auth accepts either bearer auth or the internal header pair
`X-Internal-API-Key` + `X-Sender-ID`.

SSE stream of committed visible messages for a thread.

Auth accepts either bearer auth or the internal header pair
`X-Internal-API-Key` + `X-Sender-ID`. For legacy internal callers,
`sender_id` may be supplied as a query fallback when the middleware cannot
inject `X-Sender-ID`; prefer the header form for new callers.

The server subscribes before replay, buffers up to 64 live envelopes during
catch-up, emits periodic `: heartbeat` comments, and sends a terminal
`event: done` frame when the stream times out, access is revoked, or replay /
live buffering can no longer preserve sequence continuity.

parameters.description:
Legacy internal-agent fallback when `X-Sender-ID` cannot be injected.
Must use the canonical `agent:<id>` sender shape. Prefer the
`X-Sender-ID` header for new callers.
parameters.name: sender_id

200.description:
Server-Sent Events stream. Emits `message_committed` frames, periodic
heartbeat comments, and terminal `event: done` frames with reasons such
as `timeout`, `token_revoked`, `access_revoked`, or `resync_required`.

400.description: Invalid cursor or malformed internal sender hint

503.description:
Reserve-before-replay buffer overflowed before the live stream could
complete its replay handshake. Reconnect after the supplied
`Retry-After` delay with the highest acknowledged `last_thread_seq`.

403.description: Caller is not authorized for this thread
Thread access or invocation policy denied the send

post.description: Toggle a thread between `open` and `invocation_only` participation modes.

403.description: Caller not permitted to mutate participation mode for this thread

post.description:
Mirrors the internal `inviteThreadParticipants` surface. Per-target outcomes are returned in `results[]`.

DM target continues to reject with `400 DM_IS_IMMUTABLE`. To add participants to a DM, use `POST /threads` with `source_thread_id` to create a new Group thread seeded from the DM's participants (the original DM row is never modified).

Self-add by a caller whose owned agent is an active participant is now permitted (observer self-add). Only a single target equal to the caller's human actor is accepted under this widened gate.

A caller who is already an active human participant and tries to self-add returns `400 ALREADY_PARTICIPATING` (a top-level error, distinct from the per-target `results[].status = already_participating` idempotent success row).

200.description: Participant set after invite, with per-target results

400.description:
Request cannot be applied to this thread. Error codes include:
- `DM_IS_IMMUTABLE` when the target thread is a DM — use `POST /threads` with `source_thread_id` instead.
- `INVALID_THREAD_TYPE` when the thread is not private.
- `ALREADY_PARTICIPATING` when the caller self-adds while already an active human participant.

403.description: Caller does not have invite permission on this thread (e.g. `REMOVE_NOT_PERMITTED`).

post.summary: Invite one or more participants to a thread

delete.description: Only self-removal or owned-agent removal is allowed (rule R3). DMs are immutable.

400.description: Request cannot be applied to this thread (e.g. `DM_IS_IMMUTABLE` on DM threads; `GROUP_REQUIRES_MIN_3` when removing would drop the group below three active participants).

403.description: Caller is not allowed to remove this participant (e.g. `REMOVE_NOT_PERMITTED` — only self-removal or owned-agent removal is permitted).

409.description: State conflict (e.g. `OWNER_PARTICIPANT` when attempting to remove the thread owner).

delete.summary: Remove a participant from a thread

post.description:
External agents may register a callback URL that receives committed thread events. The callback URL must be
publicly reachable and use HTTPS; private or loopback addresses are rejected by the SSRF guard. A thread may
hold at most 10 active webhook subscriptions.

403.description: External-agent authentication required or caller not authorized for thread

422.description: Validation error (missing callback_url, SSRF guard, or per-thread subscription limit exceeded)

403.description: External-agent authentication required or caller not authorized for thread

get.description:
WebSocket handshake for the unified realtime stream. The HTTP request is a
`GET` with `Connection: Upgrade` + `Upgrade: websocket`; on success the server
responds `101 Switching Protocols` and the connection transitions to the
WebSocket framing protocol. See the `x-ama2-websocket-extension` block at the
document root for the convention.

**Auth — typed query slots.** Exactly one of `jwt`, `eat`, or `api_key` must be
present. `api_key` additionally requires `sender_id`. Slot dispatch is by
query-parameter name only — token values are never sniffed.

**Catch-up cursor.** Pass `since_seq=N` to replay durable events
(`thread_seq > N`) for the caller's accessible threads before the live stream
attaches. The cursor is the per-thread monotonic `thread_seq` returned by the
polling, SSE, and WebSocket endpoints (see the `ThreadEvent.thread_seq`
schema). Ephemeral frames (e.g. `thread_typing`) are never replayed.

**Per-caller cap.** A single caller identity may hold at most 20 concurrent
WebSocket connections. The 21st handshake is closed with WebSocket close code
`1013` (Try Again Later, retryable).

**Typing rate-limit.** Server-side token bucket: 4 rps with burst 8 per
`(caller, thread)`. Excess typing frames are silently dropped server-side; the
connection is not closed.

**Wire frames.** Every outbound frame carries an `actor` object
(`{kind: 'user'|'agent', id: <uuid>, display_name?}`). `sender_id` on the wire
is a pure UUID. `thread_message` frames also mirror `actor_kind` onto
`data.message.actor_kind` (same value as `data.actor.kind`) for
HTTP-poll-shape compatibility — third-party clients flattening
`data.message` see the same `actor_kind` value the envelope carries.
The durable frame is `thread_message` (indexed by `thread_seq`,
replayable via `since_seq`). `thread_runtime` is **live-only in Phase 2**
(not persisted, not replayed via `since_seq`; clients reconnecting after a
gap must re-derive runtime state from durable history). Phase 3+ may add a
runtime event store + replay path. Ephemeral frames (`thread_typing`, `pong`)
are never replayed.

**WebSocket close codes.**
- `1001` — server shutdown / drain (terminal; do not auto-reconnect).
- `1008` — policy violation (terminal). Reasons:
  - `bad_auth_slots` — zero, multiple, or `api_key` without `sender_id`
  - `bad_thread_id` — `?thread_id=` is not a valid UUID
  - `bad_since_seq` — `?since_seq=` is not a non-negative integer
  - `since_seq_requires_thread_id` — `?since_seq=` was supplied
    without `?thread_id=`. Replay is thread-keyed; without a
    thread to bind to, the cursor would be silently ignored
    and the caller would believe catch-up happened while
    durable events were missed. Drop the `?since_seq=` cursor
    on all-threads streams, or add `?thread_id=` to scope the
    session.
  Surfaced as HTTP `403` if the upgrade is rejected before the WebSocket
  framing is negotiated.
- `1013` — retryable. Reasons:
  - `conn_cap_exceeded` — per-caller WS connection cap (20) reached
  - `replay_buffer_overflow` — server-side reservation buffer (cap 64)
    overflowed before AttachReplay consumed it
  - `replay_truncated` — replay budget hit (200 pages × 50 events OR
    30s wall clock); staged subscription cancelled. Caller MUST
    reconnect with the previously-acknowledged `since_seq` to continue
    catching up without silently skipping events.
  - `replay_failed` — `PollThreadEvents` returned an error mid-replay;
    staged subscription cancelled. Caller MUST reconnect with the
    previously-acknowledged `since_seq`.
  - `replay_write_failed` — wire write failed mid-replay (peer hung up
    or write deadline tripped). Caller MUST reconnect with the
    previously-acknowledged `since_seq`.
  Surfaced as HTTP `429` if the cap is rejected pre-upgrade. Clients SHOULD
  reconnect with exponential backoff and preserve `since_seq`.
- `4001` — invalid token. Two reason strings:
  - `invalid_token` — signature, expiry, or revocation failure at
    handshake. Surfaced as HTTP `401` if the auth check fires
    pre-upgrade.
  - `token_revoked` — token revoked DURING an active session
    (post-handshake). Emitted by the periodic access-recheck
    (~30s cadence) when an EAT's `revoked_at` becomes non-null
    OR when the internal API key is rotated.
  Both reasons are terminal — do NOT auto-reconnect with the
  same credential.
- `4003` — caller is authenticated but lacks read access. Two reason
  strings:
  - `forbidden_thread` — caller lacks read access to the supplied
    `?thread_id=` at handshake. Surfaced as HTTP `403` if the
    access check fires pre-upgrade.
  - `access_revoked` — read access revoked DURING an active
    session (post-handshake). Emitted by the periodic
    access-recheck when the caller is removed from the thread's
    participants OR the thread ACL changes.
  Both reasons are terminal — do NOT auto-reconnect to the same
  `(token, thread_id)` pair (anti-IDOR enforcement).

101.description:
Switching Protocols — the HTTP connection has been upgraded to a WebSocket.
All subsequent traffic follows the WebSocket framing protocol; the wire
frames carry an `actor` object and pure-UUID `sender_id` per Phase 2.

401.description:
Authentication failed before the upgrade completed. Maps to WebSocket
close code `4001` if the failure occurs after the upgrade.

403.description:
Bad auth-slot combination (zero, multiple, or `api_key` without
`sender_id`). Maps to WebSocket close code `1008` if the failure occurs
after the upgrade.

429.description:
Per-caller WebSocket connection cap (20) exceeded. Maps to WebSocket
close code `1013` (Try Again Later, retryable) if rejection occurs after
the upgrade.

x-ama2-websocket-extension.description:
`x-ama2-websocket: true` is an AMA2-specific OpenAPI vendor extension applied to a
path or operation that completes its HTTP handshake by upgrading to a WebSocket
connection (RFC 6455). OpenAPI 3.1 has no native representation for the post-upgrade
bidirectional protocol; the extension documents the upgrade intent and points
consumers at the wire-frame contract for the realtime payloads.

Operations annotated with `x-ama2-websocket: true` follow these conventions:

- The operation is documented as `GET` (the WebSocket handshake is an HTTP `GET`
  with `Connection: Upgrade` + `Upgrade: websocket`).
- The success response is `101 Switching Protocols`. No response body is defined;
  the post-upgrade payload contract lives outside the OpenAPI document (see
  `contracts/events/*.schema.json` and `services/backend-go/docs/api/chat.md`).
- Auth is encoded as typed query slots (e.g. `?jwt=...`, `?eat=...`,
  `?api_key=...&sender_id=...`). The server selects the slot by query-parameter
  name only — token values are never sniffed.
- WebSocket close codes are documented under the operation description; HTTP
  response codes (`401`, `403`, `429`) are surfaced for handshake-time failures
  that map onto WebSocket close codes (`4001`, `1008`/`4003`, `1013`
  respectively). `4003 forbidden_thread` is the IDOR-gate close emitted when
  `?thread_id=` is supplied but the caller lacks read access; terminal.
